rv.q: This epic might be firmly set in 2015, but it's an elegy that's teeming with a whole century of lost history – and lost lives.

The West End now has TWO era defining productions in what’s shaping up to be a golden year for London Theatre. And both shows opened in the last ten days! You can read about Marianne Elliot’s triumphant re-conception of Stephen Sondheim’s musical COMPANY here but if plays are your thing you really need to catch THE INHERITANCE at the Theatre.

When Bent first opened, AIDS was still to come. And even if it is now a (largely) treatable disease, we are still losing major gay talents to it from the theatre: the wonderful playwright Kevin Elyot (who wrote the hauntingly beautiful My Night with Reg) died in 2014, and the Broadway composer Michael Friedman (Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson) died...
